title: A meta-analysis of cognitive complexity and judgment accuracy in clinical decision making.
abstract: Cognitive complexity refers to a multidimensional information-processing style hypothesized to enhance clinical decision making. Extending the Meta-Analysis of Clinical Judgment project (Spengler et al., 2009), we reviewed 55 years of research examining the association between mental health clinicians' cognitive complexity and judgment accuracy. Nine studies (= 915) met inclusion criteria. The mean random-effects correlation was= .17 (95% CI [.11, .24],< .01) indicating a small but statistically significant positive association. Mixed effects and meta-regression moderator analyses revealed no statistically significant effects, though trends suggested stronger associations among more experienced clinicians and in higher quality studies. Findings provide modest support for cognitive complexity as a beneficial clinician characteristic while highlighting the need for further research.
